novelty.justification: The claim hypothesizes that "a mechanistic anomaly detector trained only on benign activations flags such attacks—including unseen jailbreaks—better than supervised harmful-content classifiers," with the narrower measurement prediction that "feature-co-activation anomalies are more discriminative than raw activation anomalies." Searches framed as "mechanistic anomaly detection jailbreak activations benign-only unseen attacks," "one-class jailbreak detection hidden states," and "SAE feature co-activation anomaly harmful prompts" identify close precedents: Eliciting Latent Knowledge from Quirky Language Models (2023) and Mechanistic Anomaly Detection for “Quirky” Language Models (2025) already study activation-based MAD, while LatentBiopsy (2026) is especially close in fitting a benign-only residual-stream distribution to detect harmful prompts, and RCS (2025) evaluates internal-representation jailbreak detection on unseen attack types. Moving those ideas to held-out text-jailbreak families is therefore a natural extension rather than a new core relationship; SAE co-activation graphs add a modest new operationalization, but applying anomaly scoring to another internal feature representation does not substantially change the established MAD hypothesis.
